subject: Initial discovery: inference SLA, bottlenecks, and an action roadmap
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Initial discovery: inference SLA, bottlenecks, and an action roadmap

Hi Alicia / Ravi —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track decisions:

1) Customer pain points (what you told us)
   - Intermittent 95th-percentile spikes on text-gen endpoints during peak trading hours (p95 observed 350–900ms depending on day).
   - Streaming experience in your web app is choppy for multi-turn flows — users see partial outputs arrive out of order after reconnects.
   - Cost unpredictability when fallback to public endpoints happens; want clearer unit economics and predictable commit options.

2) Current stack
   - SaaS: primary traffic hits a mix of OpenAI-hosted endpoints plus an in-house cache/proxy for prompt prefixes.
   - On deploy side: ephemeral pods behind a gateway, no consistent KV cache for KV reuse across replicas.

3) Success criteria (Finly)
   - p95 latency <= 300ms for single-turn high-priority flows, sustained at 120 qps;
   - streaming latency for first chunk <= 120ms and smooth splice for reconnections;
   - predictable monthly cost within ±10% of forecast for committed capacity.

4) Proposed immediate plan (next 2 weeks)
   - Redwood to provide: a short perf snapshot (attached) with a targeted test profile simulating your peak distribution.
   - Technical deep-dive with your infra + our SREs to map cold-start sources and KV cache placement (target week of 5/11).
   - Draft mutual action plan (MAP) for a 4-week trial on Dedicated capacity + a canary routing policy.

5) Ask from Finly
   - Can you share a representative request distribution (token lengths, percent streaming vs batch) and a short list of endpoints you consider high-priority?
   - Who on your side needs to be looped for procurement / security questionnaire (for Private/Dedicated)?

Attachments: Finly_MAP_v1.pdf (draft MAP), perf_snapshot-20270504.txt (sample perf probe results)

I copied Marissa (SE) and Neha (AM) to coordinate the technical deep-dive and commercial details. If that summary looks right I’ll: 1) schedule the 5/11 deep-dive, 2) send the MAP + trial terms for review, and 3) provision a short dedicated perf run for your traffic profile.

Thanks —
Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the clear summary. That aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- The p95 spikes are most painful between 07:30–09:30 PST (market open) and 15:30–16:30 PST (market close). During those windows we see about 130–160 concurrent inference requests for the high-priority flow.
- Streaming is ~40% of calls; when a user drops network and reconnects we often replay from the server which increases cost and results in duplicated partial chunks — that’s the UX we want to avoid.
- For procurement/security: procurement@finly.com (Ravi will loop them) + security@finly.com (we’ll share the SOC2 snapshot).

We can send the representative distribution as a CSV by EOD Thursday (5/6). Please go ahead and schedule the deep-dive. Looking forward to the MAP and trial terms.

—Alicia

Head of Product, Finly

Looping internal quick notes / proposed tech agenda for the 5/11 deep-dive:

1) Repro plan – we’ll run a targeted load test matching Finly’s peak windows (120, 140, 160 concurrent) with token-length buckets (short/medium/long) to reproduce the p95 tail.
2) Streaming watchdog – instrument first-chunk timing and reconnection splice behavior; validate that a prefix-aware KV cache reduces duplicate token emission.
3) Cold-start analysis – capture per-replica init time and KV warm-up for your current infra pattern; measure impact of continuous batching on tails.
4) Routing experiment – propose canary: 25% traffic to Redwood Dedicated with warm KV, 75% baseline for 48 hours; rollback on >10% p95 regression.

Action owners: Marissa (test harness & metrics), Karthik (schedule + procurement path), Neha (commercial & MAP).

I’ve attached a quick perf probe summary (perf_snapshot-20270504.txt) and a rough MAP draft. I’ll prepare the load script and share a runbook prior to the call.

-Marissa
